post.title: Why Xbox and PlayStation consoles are often sold at a loss
post.ig:
Microsoft testified it doesn't profit when it sells an Xbox.
In May 2021, Xbox exec Lori Wright said under oath: "We sell the consoles at a loss."
Sony's network services (mostly PlayStation Plus) grew from about ¥409B (year to March 2022) to about ¥763B (year to March 2026), while hardware sales fell about 12% that last year.
A UK lawsuit says Sony takes a 30% store cut. Our math: 30% of a $70 example game is $21. Nintendo says it tries to avoid selling hardware at a loss.
Sources: Sony Form 20-F filings, Epic v. Apple testimony (May 2021), Sony CFO via Bloomberg (Aug 2021), Nintendo IR (Feb 2026).
